title: Astra 6.2 is amazing at 3d, here's an example of it figuring out which walking animations made by opus are bad and how it fixed them for the better.
author: dantemp

comments.author: meowyih
comments.body: Obviously AI is not good at it. You can create a much better animation using Cascadeur in 5 min. Why many people insist to use AI for this? I don't think AI is any cheaper or faster.

replies.author: MesquiteBarbecueChip
replies.body: Plot twist, you can get AI to make animations in Cascadeur...

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: Would Cascadeur help with superhuman movements like attacks that include jumps that fly for meters?

replies.author: MesquiteBarbecueChip
replies.body: Most definitely, if you can move the characters pose from point A to B, it can do it

replies.author: IriFlina
replies.body: Any tips for using cascadeur? Can you do image to pose or mocap to block out the key frames in cascadeur?

comments.author: Andress1
comments.body: It's progress but they look sloppy

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: what about the animations is sloppy? If you mean the models or how they hold their props, ignore that, it's not what I'm focusing on.

replies.author: Andress1
replies.body:
They still look very robotic and not very fluid, like how a real human would move. Of course less so than the first version.

But if that's how the game is supposed to be then it's fine.

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: I have to be very sparing with model detail because the game will allow hundreds of characters on screen at the same time, but they don't have to look robotic. I guess I'm terrible judge on that stuff cause the right side looks very passable to me. But if you disagree I respect your opinion, I've never been a good judge of presentation.

replies.author: Andress1
replies.body:
For the 2005 era graphics that you have it looks like it fits the style. 

I guess it wouldn't make sense to have very fluid animations if the graphics don't match them

comments.author: Practical_Remove_682
comments.body: im literally dealing with this. i cannot find a decent way for AI to make me a running animation. Ive been at it for 2 days and I'm just about to find some asset online for a placeholder at this point lol

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: I got a decent one by [finding a reference](https://www.google.com/search?sca_esv=a72e8b939cfff0a5&rlz=1C1VDKB_enBG1094BG1094&sxsrf=AKL5yDhn8pvYq202IgCn7mnHP_Jo9gEIAw:1795173717711&udm=2&fbs=ACAhTvwdifjn2dKXmjtOfBxVFl_koHVe5RLSnJlTH2QYaq_YVfnwA0k4pzZ9d-ZbRA0e6tx_bOCeM8fujsSep3JnvBLpsc0hOB26zURjrhjv9fCML0a-BnFeEzlQgT7ikn4jRD4_oSH_c8s0RDTzS3zSUULwNZdBuzjANj-n5HV8WSg3GABsMKL5Wyawg-aQGr4_RoZm7RWj&q=sprint+animation+key+frames&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiT6oOet5aYAxW8Rv4FHQz2NLYQtKgLegQIFxAB&biw=1280&bih=585&dpr=3) for the key frames online for a sprinting animation and feeding it into Opus. It took it a bit but the final animation wasn't super bad.

replies.author: Practical_Remove_682
replies.body: oh do you just need to give it a reference? and its more likely to come out better.

comments.author: Nice_Persimmon_1266
comments.body: This is interesting. I think I've been doing a similar workflow. Are you using Astra to help prompt Opus?

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: I was building exclusively with Fable and Opus but kept being unsatisfied with graphics and presentation, decided to give astra a try and just told it to rework some of the things that I did with Claude, this is the result.

replies.author: Nice_Persimmon_1266
replies.body: I've also found that code that Codex struggled with was easily fixable with Claude. It actually seems like both are really useful when working in tandem with each other.

replies.author: dantemp
replies.body: I'm guessing it's something like that - claude for code, codex for presentation. I've had zero problems with gameplay systems built with Claude, but I use Fable max effort extensively, if it's not building it's reviewing at the very least. Gets really expensive really fast.
